CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for recent hospitalization related to spasms, lightheadedness, constipation, and diaphoresis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury presenting for follow-up after hospitalization at District Regional Hospital from 06/29/2021 to 07/02/2021. During that admission, patient presented with increasing concerns for spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. She was febrile with significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. Concerns were raised for urinary tract infection and she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She also experienced labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. She slowly improved and was discharged. Patient attributes her presentation to constipation rather than urinary tract infection, noting that she had not had a regular bowel movement in a while despite daily Miralax use. She reports that once she had a bowel movement after discharge, she felt much better. Urine cultures obtained during hospitalization were not impressive. Patient denies current pain or discomfort and reports feeling back to her normal self. She denies current complaints related to the hospitalization.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current pain or discomfort anywhere. She denies current headache, vomiting, or blood pressure concerns. She reports staying indoors more during hot weather. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury
History of constipation
Suprapubic catheter in place

MEDICATIONS
Miralax (daily, doubles dose when no bowel movement)
Lactulose (rescue therapy for severe constipation, reports it takes about 2 days to work)
Vitamin C (large amounts)
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient lives at home and tends to stay indoors more during hot and humid weather. She is somewhat homeopathic in her health approach.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, patient able to take deep breaths
General: No acute distress
Vital signs: Stable at time of visit

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization labs showed WBC 23,000 (significantly elevated). Urine cultures were not impressive. Patient's WBC has been occasionally elevated; was normal last year.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Acute to Chronic Constipation
Patient believes her recent hospitalization was more likely related to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia rather than true urinary tract infection. The elevated WBC may be related to inflammation from constipation rather than infection. Patient has good bowel regimen with Miralax as primary treatment and lactulose for severe constipation. Plan to return in 2-3 weeks for fasting laboratory work including CBC and complete metabolic panel with lipid panel. Will repeat CBC to ensure white blood cell count normalizes. Patient counseled that dehydration during hot weather can worsen constipation.

Quadriplegia
Continue current management. Patient manages well at home with suprapubic catheter.

COVID-19 Vaccine Status
Patient is unvaccinated and hesitant about vaccine due to concerns about unknown side effects and reports of vaccine injury. Discussed that she is high risk given her quadriplegia status and respiratory compromise. Recommended vaccination as the only true preventative mechanism for COVID-19. Explained that supplements and monoclonal antibodies are not reliable alternatives. Discussed that vaccines in general have rare side effects (such as Guillain-Barré), but benefits outweigh risks. Noted that approximately 50% of the country has been vaccinated. Discussed that as virus mutates, it typically becomes more contagious but less deadly. Patient remains hesitant but open-minded and will consider recommendation. Advised patient to reach out with any additional questions.
